newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end weaker but off day's lows.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end weaker but off day's lows.

text.p: Swedish shares ended lower on Monday but off the day's lows, recovered from hefty losses triggered in early trade by the dive on Wall Street on Friday.
The Stockholm general index ended 0.71 percent lower at 3,130.81 after shares worth 5.29 billion crowns changed hands.
"There was no real fall this time and I think the risk of that happening is a bit less now," said one broker.
"We are slavishly following developments in the U.S. so it became clear quite early this morning that the fall on New York was not expected to continue today," another broker said.
But brokers said they expected to see continuing volatility in the market this week.

"The market is nervous and there are a lot of expectations ahead of the interest rate policy meetings in both Germany and the U.S.. But I think that we'll get buyers back into the market once these jitters subside," said one broker.
Market heavyweights were lower. Telecoms group Ericsson fell one to 347.5 crowns while drugs major Astra was 1.5 lower at 132.5 crowns.
Construction group NCC edged up 0.5 to 90.50 crowns.
It returned to profit in the first half of 1997, posting a profit after financial items of 82 million crowns against a loss of 82 million a year ago.
The market was expecting a spate of six month reports on Tuesday, including insurer Trygg-Hansa, Handelsbanken, and mining and rubber group Trelleborg.
